steps.title: Topbar overview
steps.say: Welcome to Serpantinum! Up here is your topbar, giving you quick access to system status, workspaces, media controls, weather, time, and so on

steps.title: Left buttons
steps.say: These are quick buttons that may allow you to access some part of the system if you don't have your keybinds preconfigured, such as the help button, the app launcher and system notifications panel

steps.title: Help button
steps.say: Pressing this button will open the guide window and allow you to navigate the settings and rewatch different sections of the tutorial

steps.title: Guide popup
steps.say: This is a guide popup that will allow you to navigate the system, and it will be covered in other tutorial sections

steps.title: App search
steps.say: Pressing this button will open the app launcher that allows you to open any of the apps/programs installed on your system

steps.title: App launcher
steps.say: This is the app launcher that will be covered in another tutorial section

steps.title: Notifications button
steps.say: This bell icon opens your notifications panel, where you can review, clear, and manage anything the system or your apps have sent your way

steps.title: Notifications panel
steps.say: Here's your notification history. Anything sent by the system or your apps will show up in this list so you never miss it

steps.title: Update indicator
steps.say: Whenever a system update is available, this icon appears and gently pulses to catch your eye. Click it to open the updater and install the latest packages
exec: serpantinum close notifications && serpantinum ipc call topbar toggleUpdate && sleep 4 && serpantinum ipc call topbar toggleUpdate

steps.title: Workspaces
steps.say: These dots represent your workspaces. The highlighted one is where you currently are, and you can scroll over this area to switch between them

steps.title: Media controls
steps.say: When something is playing, this module shows the track's artwork, title, and playback time, plus buttons to skip back, play or pause, and skip forward. Click the artwork to open the full media panel

steps.title: Media panel
steps.say: This is the full media panel, with more detailed playback info and controls for whatever's currently playing

steps.title: Clock & weather
steps.say: Right in the middle you'll find the time, date, and current weather at a glance. Clicking here opens your calendar

steps.title: Calendar panel
steps.say: Here's your calendar, giving you a bigger picture view of the days, weeks, and months ahead

steps.title: System tray
steps.say: Background apps and utilities park their icons here. Left click to activate one, right click for its context menu, and middle click for a secondary action

steps.title: System pills
steps.say: This cluster of pills gives you a running readout of your keyboard layout, network, bluetooth, volume, and battery, all in one place

steps.title: Keyboard layout
steps.say: This shows your active keyboard layout. Click it to cycle to the next configured layout

steps.title: Network status
steps.say: This pill shows whether you're connected over WiFi or ethernet, along with the network name. Click it to open network settings

steps.title: Network panel
steps.say: Here you can pick a WiFi network, see signal strength, and manage saved connections

steps.title: Bluetooth status
steps.say: Here you can see your bluetooth status and any connected device. Clicking it opens the same panel on its bluetooth tab, letting you pair and manage devices

steps.title: Volume control
steps.say: This shows your current output volume. Scroll over it to adjust the level, left click to open volume settings, or right click to mute

steps.title: Volume panel
steps.say: Here you can fine-tune output and input volume levels and switch between audio devices

steps.title: Battery status
steps.say: Keep an eye on your battery charge here, colored red when low and green while charging. Click it for more detailed power information

steps.title: Battery panel
steps.say: This panel breaks down battery health, time remaining, and power usage in more detail

steps.title: Recording indicator
steps.say: This icon only appears while a screen recording is in progress. Click it to stop recording and save your screenshot or clip
exec: serpantinum screenshot --record --full && sleep 30 && pgrep -x gpu-screen-recorder >/dev/null && serpantinum screenshot

steps.title: Topbar wrap-up
steps.say: That covers the topbar! You can always revisit any of this by pressing the help button and rewatching a section from the guide
exec: pgrep -x gpu-screen-recorder >/dev/null && serpantinum screenshot; serpantinum ipc call main handleCommand close
